title: JANUS Genesis Sovereign v6.5 — Process-Global Portable Locking, Full Runtime Receipts, Controlled Default CLI, Durable Session Saga, and Fresh Revocable Trust Keys
summary: v6.5 continued the audit by attacking boundaries that v6.4 had not proved: same-process cross-instance locking on Windows, replayable full runtime receipts, active-duplicate reconciliation, default CLI request identity, durable AI-link replacement, registration request binding, provider freshness, key revocation, and cross-platform file durability. Multiple failed descendants were preserved and used to drive narrower corrections until the final v18.7.35 acceptance run passed on both Ubuntu and Windows.

A13_same_process_cross_instance_lock.pre_fix: PortableProcessLock v1 used one Python RLock per lock object, so the Windows same-process cross-instance claim was not established. The old lifecycle test also placed a Barrier inside the critical section and therefore did not prove the intended exclusion property.
A13_same_process_cross_instance_lock.response: janus_portable_lock_v2.py uses a process-global canonical-path RLock plus an OS lock. A new deterministic test places synchronization outside the critical section and measures maximum overlap.

A14_legacy_v25_sqlite_lifetime.pre_fix: Historical SQLiteEffectFenceStore still contains sqlite context-manager patterns that were not migrated by the v29 focused fix.
A14_legacy_v25_sqlite_lifetime.response: v31 introduced a separate portable runtime-request store with explicit connection ownership; legacy v25 was not silently relabeled portable.

A15_ai_link_durable_replace.pre_fix: Base AI-link JSON replacement used one fixed .tmp path without fsync or directory durability semantics.
A15_ai_link_durable_replace.response: v32 introduced unique same-directory temporary files, temp fsync, replacement, final-file fsync, and POSIX directory fsync. v35 corrected the Windows final-file fsync descriptor contract.

A16_cross_store_registration.pre_fix: World registration occurred before session persistence, allowing an invisible world-first partial state after crash.
A16_cross_store_registration.response: v32 writes PENDING_WORLD_REGISTRATION before authoritative world registration; v34 durably binds registration_request_id to one normalized registration before the saga. Retry can reconcile a visible pending state.

A17_default_cli_raw_process_action.pre_fix: play_genesis.py interactive actions and --action called world.process_action directly.
A17_default_cli_raw_process_action.response: Default normal process_action entries now route through the v18.7.33 descendant with stable request IDs, full receipts, --request-id, --request-state, and interactive /retry.

A18_hash_only_settlement.pre_fix: Earlier client settlement stored only result_sha256 and therefore could not replay a completed result without re-entering runtime.
A18_hash_only_settlement.response: v31 stores canonical full result_json plus result_sha256 and reconstructs WorldResult from the receipt. SETTLED replay does not call the world again.

A19_provider_freshness_and_replay.pre_fix: Authorization-bound signed provider evidence had no age, expiry, key lifecycle, or nonce-reuse policy.
A19_provider_freshness_and_replay.response: v32 introduced observed_at_tick, expires_at_tick, max-age enforcement, durable key eligibility, revocation, generation, and an idempotent nonce-to-payload binding. v34 corrected the typed outcome implementation bug.

A20_lineage_key_lifecycle.pre_fix: A valid historical HMAC key remained indistinguishable from a currently eligible key.
A20_lineage_key_lifecycle.response: TrustKeyRegistry records purpose, generation, not-before, not-after, and revocation. Origin and reviewer attestations must verify under current policy.

A21_thread_vs_process_evidence.pre_fix: Two lock objects in threads and two processes had been conflated as one portability claim.
A21_thread_vs_process_evidence.response: v2 gates separately test same-process distinct instances, nonblocking local contention, and spawned-process contention.

A22_multi_host_boundary.note: Process-global plus OS locking remains same-host/shared-filesystem coordination, not distributed consensus.

A23_forced_exit_and_other_mutators.finding: The new default CLI protection explicitly covers normal process_action entries. force_exit, save import/export, display-name mutation, and network publication have distinct mutation semantics and are not silently covered by the runtime receipt claim.
